definitions.explanation: A short, memorable saying that expresses a general truth or piece of advice. Often attributed to a specific person or tradition.

examples.japanese: ⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{格言|かくげん}だ。
⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧{格言|かくげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引用|いんよう}して→引用する：26928_inyousuru⟧⟦{話|はな}した→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather often spoke by quoting proverbs.

examples.japanese: 「{時|とき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{金|かね}→金：02618_kane⟧なり」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧{格言|かくげん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{世界中|せかいじゅう}→世界中：10171_sekaijuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: The maxim 'time is money' is known throughout the world.

notes: Distinguished from related words: ⟦{諺|ことわざ}→諺：02765_kotowaza⟧ (proverb) refers to folk sayings passed down through generations, while {格言|かくげん} tends to refer to more literary or attributed sayings. ⟦{名言|めいげん}→名言：20185_meigen⟧ (famous saying) emphasizes that the quote is well-known and often attributed to a specific person. Common collocations include {格言|かくげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引用|いんよう}する→引用する：26928_inyousuru⟧ (to quote an aphorism) and {格言|かくげん}{集|しゅう} (collection of maxims).
